rejected.why: Viewed 2026-07-30. Titled 'harbour' but there is no harbour in it — the lower half of the frame is flat wet grey sand and a set of bare concrete steps, with the town on the ridge behind. Nothing that says working port. Replaced by luderitz-harbour-2002.webp and luderitz-harbour-quay.webp.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Subject incidental: a single small white church sits on the far skyline while roughly 45 per cent of the frame is empty blue sky and 45 per cent is bare dirt scattered with litter and a fallen pipe. It shows none of the German colonial townscape the caption promised.

Viewed 2026-07-30. A washed-out hazy frame of one anonymous grey rock hump with flat white sky above it. It gives no sense of Shark Island's shape or of what happened there. The other Shark Island frame was kept.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Fetched as an interior; it is an exterior overview in which the buildings are a thin distant strip and about 60 per cent of the frame is featureless rippled sand. Both the caption and the composition failed.

Viewed 2026-07-30. A faded 2002 slide scan with a heavy pink cast: four tiny houses on a distant sand ridge, everything below them empty flat sand. The signature sight of this port deserves better than a speck on the horizon.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Not a readable bridge — a tight crop of broken splintered timbers and a rail against blank sky, with no ground, no sea and no context. A reader could not tell what they were looking at.
Viewed 2026-07-30. One flamingo occupies well under one per cent of a wide seascape of surf and kelp-covered rock; at page size the bird disappears. Replaced by luderitz-flamingo-radford-bay.webp.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Fetched as a harbour frame; more than half the picture is rubble-strewn rock waste ground in the foreground, the water is a thin band, and the only structures are a hotel and some sheds. No quay, no shipping. Replaced by luderitz-harbour-quay.webp.
Viewed 2026-07-30. The lower half of the frame is empty tarmac road and gravel verge; the town is a distant band of small houses with no colonial architecture legible. Not usable as a townscape.

Viewed 2026-07-30. This is the classic Kolmanskop picture — sand drifted through two doorways in a blue-and-green painted room — and it is exactly on subject, but it carries a burned-in '500px' watermark across the bottom-left corner. We do not publish defaced files. Replaced by luderitz-kolmanskop-7.webp.
